# HyperFrames Motion Craft — Measured from Official Films

Adapted from `heygen-com/hyperframes` `skills/hyperframes/references/motion.md`.
All values measured frame-by-frame from the official HyperFrames launch films.

These are defaults. A reference the user provides, or a scene that deliberately does otherwise, wins for its own beat.

---

## Core Motion Rules

### Speed and Duration
- **A fast move takes 0.3–0.6 s** with motion blur on its own ease, peaking at its fastest frame
- **Motion blur**: 6–12 px on text-sized elements, 15–20 px full-frame, horizontal-only on horizontal moves
- **Render-time blur**: `data-motion-blur="on"` on the composition root smears moving elements along their real path (opt-in)

### Arrival vs Departure
- **Arrive slow, leave clean**: long-tailed ease-outs on arrivals; landing takes longer than leaving
- An exit is one smooth motion — never slide, stop, then leave
- Entrances that are too snappy read as glitches; slowing by ~1 second often fixes it

### Ease by Role

| Role | Ease |
|------|------|
| Arrival / landing | `expo.out`, `power4.out` (long tail) |
| Camera move / colour flood | `power2.inOut` (both ways) |
| Zoom through / exit | `power3.in` (accelerates out) |
| Rotation / progress bar | `linear` |

The same `power2.out` at 0.5 s on **everything** is the flat default that makes a film feel generated.

### Springs

Springs are named by damping ratio:

| Damping | Feel |
|---------|------|
| 1.0 | Never bounces — dead landing |
| 0.7–0.85 | Reads premium |
| 0.4–0.6 | Playful |
| < 0.3 | Cartoon |

- Position and size **may** bounce; opacity and colour **never** bounce
- GSAP equivalents: `elastic.out(1, 0.5)` and `back.out(1.4)`
- A closed-form spring of `t` keeps any frame renderable on its own (deterministic)

```javascript
// FrameForge engine.js — spring with damping ratio control
spring(t, { tension: 200, friction: 20 })   // damping ≈ 0.7 (premium)
spring(t, { tension: 300, friction: 10 })   // damping ≈ 0.3 (cartoon)
spring(t, { tension: 120, friction: 28 })   // damping ≈ 1.0 (dead)
```

### Timing Relationships
- **Exits are 40–50% shorter** than their entrances
- **Overlap**: the next element starts when the previous is 30–50% done — fully sequential looks robotic, all-at-once looks cheap
- **Stagger**: letters a frame apart, words 60–120 ms, list items 40–80 ms

### Beat Grid
- Frames per beat = `fps × 60 / BPM`
- Compute each beat from its **index** and round it — never add rounded beats repeatedly (at 128 BPM and 30 fps that drifts 2 frames in 32 beats)
- Cut on the beat; change the layout on the bar

### Cuts
- Cut at the **fastest frame** of a move, with matching direction and speed on both sides
- A click into a new screen is a match cut on the click's rebound — the new screen comes in slightly large and settles

---

## Title Animation Patterns

A landed title is **dead still** — the motion moves to the next element, the camera, or the world behind. Vary the entrance within a film.

| Pattern | How |
|---------|-----|
| Per word blur-in | `blur(6px)` → 0 and opacity 0 → 1 in 0.13 s, 0.067 s apart, no translate |
| Per word colour | Light grey → ink, 0.07–0.1 s apart, no position change |
| Whole line blur | 8 px → 0 in 0.13–0.2 s |
| Per letter name | 0.1 s apart, opacity 0.3 → 1, slight blur |
| Slot machine | One word rolls through options, ~0.1 s a roll |
| Behind subject | Title between the plate and a matte of the person |

### Hold Times
- A line the viewer must read holds **0.5 s + 0.3 s per word**
- The film's last line: **at least 2 s**
- A one- or two-word chapter line: **0.4 s**
- Exit: blur-out and fade 0.13–0.25 s word by word, or with the scene's move

### Title Sizes
- Body: 4–9% of frame height, one or two lines
- Quiet lines: 2.5–4% against hero words that fill 60–90% of width
- One highlighted word in the accent colour (carries meaning)

---

## Rhythm

| Pattern | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Montage cuts | Every 0.13–0.8 s |
| Demo hold | 7–10 s while UI acts |
| Average shot | 1.8–3 s with motion inside |
| Pre-payoff hold | 0.3–0.75 s before the payoff |
| Payoff speed | Normal speed (not slow) |

**Continuous motion that works**: UI working, footage playing, character acting, 3D world turning, slow orbit of background stage (3–5° per second).

**Defaults that look generated**:
- Breathing/floating/pulsing loops on titles and UI
- Titles that keep sliding or scaling after they land
- A slow creeping scale or push late in a scene
- Bounce on UI elements
- Click rings
- Every scene entering the same way
- Every element fading and sliding up

---

## Transitions with a Cause

Use 3–5 kinds in a film, each **caused by something on screen**. Hard cuts belong inside a scene (punch-ins); at most a third of seams between beats are hard cuts. Worlds never crossfade.

| Transition | How to Build |
|------------|-------------|
| Zoom through a button | Camera tracks to button with blur (0.6 s), button scales from ~8% to ~250% of frame in 0.35 s, strong ease-in; its fill becomes the next frame |
| Object becomes the world | Pill or card grows past the frame in 0.65 s ease-in-out, radius shrinks; what was around it blurs ~15 px and fades in 0.3 s; new content fades in while still growing |
| Morph | One container widens into the next (~110 → ~880 px in 0.2 s `power3.out`) with horizontal blur 12 → 0 |
| Carry across | Result shrinks 1 → 0.6 with blur peaking at 6 px mid-move, lands inside the next app as it builds around it |
| Colour flood | Hero object stays while the whole ground changes colour in ~0.4 s `power2.inOut` |
| Whip | Horizontal or vertical smear of 0.13–0.3 s; arriving element lands blurred and sharpens in ~0.13 s |
| Iris from click | `clip-path: circle()` opens from the clicked point onto the next world in 0.15 s |
| Dip cut | Outgoing frame darkens ~40% for 3 frames before a hard cut, so the cut reads as intentional |
| Blur swap | Out: opacity → 0 with ~8 px blur in 0.13–0.2 s; in: blur → 0 in 0.13 s; ground never cuts |

---

## The Right Mechanism for Camera Moves

| Request | Mechanism |
|---------|-----------|
| Punch-in, zoom, pan, Ken Burns, reframe | Tween `scale` and `x`/`y` on a **wrapper inside** the clip — never on the timed media element |
| Crop or mask reveal | Tween `clip-path` or mask on an inner wrapper; source time untouched |
| Constant speed change | `data-playback-rate` on the media (0.1–10) |
| Speed ramp | `rate` lane in `data-automation` on the media |
| Hold or freeze | Hold a final frame; a freeze mid-source needs a still exported first |

---

## Sound (HyperFrames/Earshot Standard)

Sound is half of how a film feels.

### The Default
- **A film over ~15 s** that tells something gets a music bed and sounds on its visible actions — unless the person asked for silence
- **Each storyline says its sound** in one line: the bed's feel and tempo, the one moment the music changes, which actions get effects

### The Clock
- **Narrated**: the voice is the clock — time each beat's start to its anchor word
- **Music only**: the music is the clock — land the payoff on strong beats; cuts follow motion, not the drums

### Effects: Few and Exact

Every effect has a cause on screen. Too many read as a template.

| Sound | Only on |
|-------|---------|
| click | A real cursor click on screen |
| whoosh | A scene cut, or a large card moving fast |
| soft key tick | Text arriving letter by letter or line by line |
| pop | A badge, chip, or number landing |
| riser into impact | The payoff or the mark — **once in the film** |

- Sound peak lands **one frame after** its picture (light arrives before sound)
- Each hit sits **3–6 dB over the bed**
- Rotate 2–3 takes of a repeated sound — the same whoosh on every cut is the most common tell
- No synthesized tones, chimes, or dings

### Levels
- Music under a voice: ~0.14 volume (≈ −17 dB relative)
- Target loudness: **−16 to −14 LUFS** (social/web)
- True peak: **−1 dBTP** or lower
- Check with `npx hyperframes audio <video> --json` equivalent: use earshot `measure` or ffmpeg `-filter loudnorm`

---

## Common Faults and Fixes

| Symptom | Cause |
|---------|-------|
| Blank or frozen scene | Timeline registered before async build finished, or `visibility` tweened on a `.clip` |
| Stutter or drift between renders | Layout measured in `onUpdate`, `requestAnimationFrame`, or clock time |
| Jump at a cut | Outgoing and incoming states differ at the seam |
| Ease looks off at a handoff | Speeds don't match across the seam — mirror the ease (`power3.in` out, `power3.out` in) |

# Motion Craft Reference — 10 Hard Motion Craft Rules

This guide defines the production motion design standards implemented across FrameForge and the HTML-as-compositor rendering pipeline.

---

## 1. Springs, Not Linear Easing
Real physical motion never moves at constant velocity or abrupt linear ramps. Every entrance and transition must model a damped harmonic oscillator:

$$\ddot{x} + 2\zeta\omega\dot{x} + \omega^2 x = 0$$

- **Default tension**: `160 - 200`
- **Default friction**: `13 - 16`
- **Closed-form function**: `spring(t, delay, tension, friction)` maps pure time $t$ to normalized displacement $[0, 1]$ with natural overshoot and settling.

---

## 2. Three-Property Entrances
Never animate a single property (such as opacity alone or scale alone). High-production visuals orchestrate three coordinated properties for every entering entity:
1. **Scale**: $0.88 \to 1.0$ (spatial arrival)
2. **Opacity**: $0.0 \to 1.0$ (perceptual fade)
3. **Translation**: $Y: +40\text{px} \to 0\text{px}$ or $X: \pm 60\text{px} \to 0\text{px}$ (directional momentum)

---

## 3. Staggered Entrance Choreography
Never trigger all elements simultaneously. When rendering cards, list items, or diagram nodes:
- Stagger siblings by $0.15\text{s} - 0.28\text{s}$ relative to base timestamp.
- Hierarchy flows from primary anchor $\to$ structural components $\to$ explanatory callouts $\to$ micro-badges.

---

## 4. Asymmetric Timing: Exits Faster Than Entrances
- **Entrances**: Informative, welcoming, gentle settling ($0.5\text{s} - 0.8\text{s}$ duration).
- **Exits**: Crisp, decisive, purposeful ($0.2\text{s} - 0.35\text{s}$ duration). Exits must clear the stage without lingering.

---

## 5. Five-Layer Depth Stack
Every scene must maintain clear atmospheric depth across 5 distinct visual layers:
- **Layer 1: Ambient Backdrop** — Radial gradients, atmospheric tint, depth falloff.
- **Layer 2: Environment / Context** — Architectural wainscoting, blueprint grid, floor plane, distant mountain ridges, or starry cosmos.
- **Layer 3: Primary Visual Entity** — The core subject (doodle character, cutaway engine, split comparison cards, neural insight core, or optical loupe).
- **Layer 4: Explanatory Callouts & Overlays** — Connecting vector lines, animated pulse packets, telemetry tags, and indicator badges.
- **Layer 5: Foreground Framing & Vignette** — Subtle radial corner shading, specular glass arcs, or foreground foliage.

---

## 6. Continuous Audio-Driven Camera Progression
Scenes must never switch camera angles at arbitrary fixed timer intervals. Camera motion is a continuous parametric function of speech duration:

$$p = \frac{t}{\text{DURATION}}$$

- **Dynamic zoom**: $1.0 + p \times 0.08$
- **Dynamic pan**: Organic Lissajous drift ($\sin(0.4t) \times 6\text{px}$)
- **Cut synchronization**: Scene cuts occur strictly on spoken sentence boundaries and audio cues.

---

## 7. Continuous Life (Zero Frozen PowerPoint Slides)
Every frame must contain subtle life. An audience detects static images instantly:
- Rotating gears ($t \times \omega$)
- Oscillating telemetry needles and wave pulses
- Flowing data packets along pipeline tracks
- Gentle character breathing and foliage sway ($\sin(3t) \times 4\text{px}$)

---

## 8. Hand-Drawn Boil Wobble at 12fps
When rendering hand-drawn doodle characters and sketch line work, apply authentic 12fps line boil wobble:
- Quantize step to 12fps: `step = Math.floor(t * 12)`
- Use seeded deterministic trigonometric noise:
  `Math.sin(seed * 19.37 + step * 2.41) * 2.4`
- Never use `Math.random()` inside the render loop.

---

## 9. Regional Typography & HarfBuzz Text Shaping
Ensure professional typographic hierarchy:
- Auto-detect script (Malayalam: Manjari / Gayathri / Chilanka; Devanagari: Noto Sans Devanagari; Latin: Inter / Rajdhani / Cinzel).
- Maintain WCAG AAA contrast ratios against backgrounds.
- Gate on-screen subtitles: display narration text only when explicitly requested in prompt.

---

## 10. Closed-Loop Visual QA Gate
Never deliver rendered video blind. The production harness must execute automated quality checks across 4 axes:
1. **Content Presence**: Non-blank ($> 1.5\%$ foreground variance).
2. **Luminance / Exposure**: Non-blown ($< 96\%$ overexposure).
3. **Compositional Distribution**: Not corner-confined ($> 12\%$ bbox coverage).
4. **Motion Delta Verification**: Test frame delta between $t = 30\%$ and $t = 70\%$ to guarantee continuous animation.

# OneTake Continuous Camera Choreography

Derived from `feitangyuan/onetake`. Eliminates abrupt black cuts, slideshow jumps, and disconnected slide transitions.

---

## The OneTake Principle

In standard presentation videos, scene transitions cut to black or snap immediately between unrelated slide geometries. In **OneTake**, the entire video occurs within a single, continuous, unified spatial universe:

$$\text{Camera}(t) = \text{Spline}(\mathbf{P}_0, \mathbf{P}_1, \dots, \mathbf{P}_N, t)$$

Every scene's starting camera transform $(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}, \text{zoom})$ is identically anchored to the previous scene's terminating transform.

---

## 1. Unified Spatial Canvas

Instead of unmounting and mounting DOM elements per scene, the entire video timeline exists on a 2.5D coordinate plane:

- **Scene 1 (Hook)**: Positioned at $(0, 0)$, Zoom $= 1.0$
- **Scene 2 (Mechanism)**: Positioned at $(1920, 0)$, Zoom $= 1.15$
- **Scene 3 (Zoom Detail)**: Positioned at $(1920, 400)$, Zoom $= 1.80$
- **Scene 4 (Wide Resolution)**: Positioned at $(960, 200)$, Zoom $= 0.85$

---

## 2. Spring-Interpolated Camera Navigation

When moving from Scene $k$ to Scene $k+1$:
1. **Never use linear interpolation**.
2. **Use underdamped spring physics** with slight overshoot:
   - Tension: `140`
   - Friction: `14`
3. **Camera Lead / Look-Ahead**:
   $$\text{CameraTarget}(t) = \text{SubjectPos}(t) + \mathbf{v}_{\text{subject}} \times 0.25$$

---

## 3. Depth-Parallax Layering

During continuous camera travel, layers shift at varying rates proportional to depth $z$:

| Layer | Depth $z$ | Parallax Factor | Visual Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Background Grid | $z = 0.2$ | $0.2 \times \Delta x$ | Blueprint grid, starfield, faint topographical lines |
| Middle Ground | $z = 0.6$ | $0.6 \times \Delta x$ | Secondary cards, connecting vector pipes, data nodes |
| Primary Stage | $z = 1.0$ | $1.0 \times \Delta x$ | Main subject, active text card, character avatar |
| Foreground Overlay | $z = 1.4$ | $1.4 \times \Delta x$ | Lens vignette, framing pillars, floating particles |

---

## 4. Zero-Cut Scene Handshake Contract

When transitioning between narrative beats:
- The outgoing scene subject smoothly settles into a secondary supporting node (e.g., shifts left to $x = 300\text{px}$ and scales down to $0.65$).
- The incoming scene subject enters from depth ($z = 0.5 \to 1.0$) rather than snapping onto the screen.
- A whoosh sound effect from `Leonxlnx/earshot` fires at the exact inflection point of peak camera velocity.

# Render Contract — Deterministic Frame Specification

This document specifies the strict mathematical and runtime contract required for all FrameForge HTML-as-compositor rendering engines.

---

## 1. Pure Mathematical Function of Time: $F(t) \to \text{Pixels}$

Every scene page must behave as a pure, stateless function of time $t$ in seconds:

$$\text{Frame}(t) = \mathcal{R}(\text{SceneState}(t))$$

- **Zero Memory Leaks**: Frame $N$ must never depend on whether Frame $N-1$ was previously rendered.
- **Out-of-Order Parallelism**: Frames can be rendered out of sequence across multiple worker threads (e.g. Worker 1 renders $t=1.0\text{s}$, Worker 2 renders $t=0.2\text{s}$, Worker 3 renders $t=2.5\text{s}$).

---

## 2. Virtual Clock Interception

The harness injects a virtual clock prior to page script execution (`capture.mjs`):

- **Overridden APIs**:
  - `window.performance.now()` $\to$ returns $t \times 1000$
  - `Date.now()` $\to$ returns `virtualEpoch + t * 1000`
  - `window.Date` constructor $\to$ anchored to `VirtualDate(t)`
  - `requestAnimationFrame(cb)` $\to$ registered into a synchronized callback queue
  - `CSS Animations` $\to$ synced via `document.getAnimations().forEach(a => a.currentTime = t * 1000)`

---

## 3. Seeded PRNG Determinism Invariant

Standard `Math.random()` produces divergent frames on repeated renders and breaks cache hashing.
- **Forbidden**: `Math.random()`
- **Required**: Seeded PRNG (`sfc32` or deterministic integer hashing).
- **Time-Synchronized Reseed**:
  ```javascript
  let _seed = (0x2F6E2B1 ^ Math.imul(Math.floor(t * 1000), 0x9E3779B9)) | 0;
  function prng() {
    _seed = (_seed + 0x6D2B79F5) | 0;
    let x = Math.imul(_seed ^ (_seed >>> 15), 1 | _seed);
    x = (x + Math.imul(x ^ (x >>> 7), 61 | x)) ^ x;
    return ((x ^ (x >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  }
  ```

---

## 4. Three-Point Purity Gate (`verify-purity.mjs`)

Every scene must pass the 3-point purity gate prior to full-rate production encoding:
1. **Repeat Check**: Sampling $t = 1.0\text{s}$ twice in succession must yield identical SHA-256 frame hashes.
2. **Wander Check**: Seeking forward $0\text{s} \to 2.5\text{s}$ and then jumping back to $1.0\text{s}$ must yield the identical hash as the cold seek.
3. **Cold Jump Check**: Spawning a fresh browser session and seeking immediately to $1.0\text{s}$ must match the sequential seek.

---

## 5. Master Encoding Contract (`encode.mjs`)

Output MP4s must comply with broadcast and streaming color standards:
- **Codec**: `libx264` (Profile: High, Level: 4.2)
- **Pixel Format**: `yuv420p`
- **Color Matrix**: `BT.709` tags:
  `-colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -color_range tv`
- **Audio Synchronization**: Exact audio mux with 18dB voiceover sidechain ducking.

# Motion Craft Reference — 10 Hard Motion Craft Rules

This guide defines the production motion design standards implemented across FrameForge and the HTML-as-compositor rendering pipeline.

---

## 1. Springs, Not Linear Easing
Real physical motion never moves at constant velocity or abrupt linear ramps. Every entrance and transition must model a damped harmonic oscillator:

$$\ddot{x} + 2\zeta\omega\dot{x} + \omega^2 x = 0$$

- **Default tension**: `160 - 200`
- **Default friction**: `13 - 16`
- **Closed-form function**: `spring(t, delay, tension, friction)` maps pure time $t$ to normalized displacement $[0, 1]$ with natural overshoot and settling.

---

## 2. Three-Property Entrances
Never animate a single property (such as opacity alone or scale alone). High-production visuals orchestrate three coordinated properties for every entering entity:
1. **Scale**: $0.88 \to 1.0$ (spatial arrival)
2. **Opacity**: $0.0 \to 1.0$ (perceptual fade)
3. **Translation**: $Y: +40\text{px} \to 0\text{px}$ or $X: \pm 60\text{px} \to 0\text{px}$ (directional momentum)

---

## 3. Staggered Entrance Choreography
Never trigger all elements simultaneously. When rendering cards, list items, or diagram nodes:
- Stagger siblings by $0.15\text{s} - 0.28\text{s}$ relative to base timestamp.
- Hierarchy flows from primary anchor $\to$ structural components $\to$ explanatory callouts $\to$ micro-badges.

---

## 4. Asymmetric Timing: Exits Faster Than Entrances
- **Entrances**: Informative, welcoming, gentle settling ($0.5\text{s} - 0.8\text{s}$ duration).
- **Exits**: Crisp, decisive, purposeful ($0.2\text{s} - 0.35\text{s}$ duration). Exits must clear the stage without lingering.

---

## 5. Five-Layer Depth Stack
Every scene must maintain clear atmospheric depth across 5 distinct visual layers:
- **Layer 1: Ambient Backdrop** — Radial gradients, atmospheric tint, depth falloff.
- **Layer 2: Environment / Context** — Architectural wainscoting, blueprint grid, floor plane, distant mountain ridges, or starry cosmos.
- **Layer 3: Primary Visual Entity** — The core subject (doodle character, cutaway engine, split comparison cards, neural insight core, or optical loupe).
- **Layer 4: Explanatory Callouts & Overlays** — Connecting vector lines, animated pulse packets, telemetry tags, and indicator badges.
- **Layer 5: Foreground Framing & Vignette** — Subtle radial corner shading, specular glass arcs, or foreground foliage.

---

## 6. Continuous Audio-Driven Camera Progression
Scenes must never switch camera angles at arbitrary fixed timer intervals. Camera motion is a continuous parametric function of speech duration:

$$p = \frac{t}{\text{DURATION}}$$

- **Dynamic zoom**: $1.0 + p \times 0.08$
- **Dynamic pan**: Organic Lissajous drift ($\sin(0.4t) \times 6\text{px}$)
- **Cut synchronization**: Scene cuts occur strictly on spoken sentence boundaries and audio cues.

---

## 7. Continuous Life (Zero Frozen PowerPoint Slides)
Every frame must contain subtle life. An audience detects static images instantly:
- Rotating gears ($t \times \omega$)
- Oscillating telemetry needles and wave pulses
- Flowing data packets along pipeline tracks
- Gentle character breathing and foliage sway ($\sin(3t) \times 4\text{px}$)

---

## 8. Hand-Drawn Boil Wobble at 12fps
When rendering hand-drawn doodle characters and sketch line work, apply authentic 12fps line boil wobble:
- Quantize step to 12fps: `step = Math.floor(t * 12)`
- Use seeded deterministic trigonometric noise:
  `Math.sin(seed * 19.37 + step * 2.41) * 2.4`
- Never use `Math.random()` inside the render loop.

---

## 9. Regional Typography & HarfBuzz Text Shaping
Ensure professional typographic hierarchy:
- Auto-detect script (Malayalam: Manjari / Gayathri / Chilanka; Devanagari: Noto Sans Devanagari; Latin: Inter / Rajdhani / Cinzel).
- Maintain WCAG AAA contrast ratios against backgrounds.
- Gate on-screen subtitles: display narration text only when explicitly requested in prompt.

---

## 10. Closed-Loop Visual QA Gate
Never deliver rendered video blind. The production harness must execute automated quality checks across 4 axes:
1. **Content Presence**: Non-blank ($> 1.5\%$ foreground variance).
2. **Luminance / Exposure**: Non-blown ($< 96\%$ overexposure).
3. **Compositional Distribution**: Not corner-confined ($> 12\%$ bbox coverage).
4. **Motion Delta Verification**: Test frame delta between $t = 30\%$ and $t = 70\%$ to guarantee continuous animation.

  ```javascript
    let x = Math.imul(_seed ^ (_seed >>> 15), 1 | _seed);
    x = (x + Math.imul(x ^ (x >>> 7), 61 | x)) ^ x;
    return ((x ^ (x >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  }
  ```

---

## 4. Three-Point Purity Gate (`verify-purity.mjs`)

Every scene must pass the 3-point purity gate prior to full-rate production encoding:
1. **Repeat Check**: Sampling $t = 1.0\text{s}$ twice in succession must yield identical SHA-256 frame hashes.
2. **Wander Check**: Seeking forward $0\text{s} \to 2.5\text{s}$ and then jumping back to $1.0\text{s}$ must yield the identical hash as the cold seek.
3. **Cold Jump Check**: Spawning a fresh browser session and seeking immediately to $1.0\text{s}$ must match the sequential seek.

---

## 5. Master Encoding Contract (`encode.mjs`)

Output MP4s must comply with broadcast and streaming color standards:
- **Codec**: `libx264` (Profile: High, Level: 4.2)
- **Pixel Format**: `yuv420p`
- **Color Matrix**: `BT.709` tags:
  `-colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -color_range tv`
- **Audio Synchronization**: Exact audio mux with 18dB voiceover sidechain ducking.

# ANIMATION_GUIDE.md — Agent Context for HTML Video Projects

> This file is loaded as context by the model before it writes any scene code.
> It encodes the contract, the four storyboard gates, and the six determinism rules
> that make headless-Chrome rendering reproducible and parallel.
>
> Source: ClaudeAnimationBase ANIMATION_GUIDE.md + awesomeclaude.ai corpus study (703 prompts).

---

## The Contract

A video is a set of scene files where **every pixel is a pure function of time `t`**.

The renderer owns the clock. Scenes never call `Date.now()`, `performance.now()`,
`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `Math.random()`, or any module-level mutable counter.
The renderer injects a virtual clock shim before the page loads, advances it one frame
at a time, and screenshots the result. Frame 400 can be captured hours after frame 399
and the scene must not care.

---

## Step 0 — Beat Sheet First

**Never write scene code before the storyboard passes all four gates.**

The workflow is always:

1. Write a beat sheet (title, shots, events, reads, transitions).
2. Reply with the beat sheet and four keyframe descriptions **only**. Stop.
3. Wait for approval.
4. Only after approval: write the scene files.

Fixing a line in a beat sheet costs one message. Fixing a finished scene costs a rewrite.

---

## The Four Storyboard Gates

Run `node scripts/storyboard-validator.mjs STORYBOARD.md` to enforce these automatically.

### Gate 1 — Every shot has an EVENT

An event is something that **physically happens** in the shot. It is not a description
of what the viewer sees, and it is not a mood adjective.

| ❌ FAILS | ✅ PASSES |
|---|---|
| "Clawd stands in a meadow." | "Clawd turns to face the viewer and extends one hand." |
| "A beautiful space scene." | "A comet crosses the frame left-to-right over 4 seconds." |
| "We see the city at night." | "The city's lights flicker off one by one from the edges in." |

### Gate 2 — Reads must not overlap

Each shot has a list of **reads** — the discrete things a viewer must understand,
with non-overlapping start and end timestamps.

```
# BAD — 0.0–1.5 and 1.0–2.5 overlap from 1.0–1.5
reads:
  - 0.0–1.5: Viewer recognises the character.
  - 1.0–2.5: Viewer understands she is running away.

# GOOD
reads:
  - 0.0–2.0: Viewer recognises the character.
  - 2.0–4.0: Viewer understands she is running away.
```

### Gate 3 — Every seam has a named transition

This includes the film open (transition_in on Shot 1) and film close
(transition_out on the last shot). A storyboard that starts or ends
without a declared transition fails.

Recognised transition names:
`cut` `fade-from-black` `fade-to-black` `dissolve` `wipe-left` `wipe-right`
`iris-in` `iris-out` `cross-dissolve` `push-left` `push-right` `flash` `dip-to-white`

### Gate 4 — No text on screen

"Lost" must be acted, not captioned. "Heartbroken" must be shown, not written.

The model **may not** write `text()`, `wallCard()`, `stamp()`, or `codeCard()` calls
that convey plot-critical information (character names, place names, dates, emotions,
narrative exposition). These helpers exist for UI/diagram/explainer content only,
not for storytelling that belongs in the direction.

---

## Six Determinism Rules

These rules are what make the render reproducible, parallel, and resumable.

### Rule 1 — Read time, never count frames

```js
// ❌ BAD — frame counter mutates across calls
let frame = 0
layer('x').on(() => { frame++; return { opacity: frame / 30 } })

// ✅ GOOD — pure function of t
layer('x').on(t => ({ opacity: Math.min(1, t / 1.0) }))
```

### Rule 2 — Seed everything with `hash(i)`

`hash(i)` in `reel/engine.js` is a deterministic integer hash of its index.
Use it wherever you need a stable pseudo-random value (star positions, brush seeds,
particle offsets). Never use `Math.random()` inside a scene file.

```js
import { hash } from './reel/engine.js'

// Star field — same every render
for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) {
  const x = (hash(i)     % 1920)
  const y = (hash(i + 1) % 1080)
  // ...
}
```

**Boil wobble exception:** hand-drawn wobble is deliberately re-seeded 12 times
per second so it looks chaotic while remaining reproducible:

```js
const boilSeed = Math.floor(t * 12) // same bucket for every frame in that 1/12s window
const wobble   = (hash(boilSeed) % 7) - 3  // –3 to +3 px
```

### Rule 3 — No integrating physics

Never integrate velocity per tick. Use closed-form motion or precompute the
simulation into an array before the layer is registered.

```js
// ❌ BAD — position depends on previous frame
let vx = 0, x = 0
layer('ball').on(() => { vx += 0.1; x += vx; return { left: x } })

// ✅ GOOD — closed-form quadratic
layer('ball').on(t => ({ left: 0.5 * 120 * t * t + 'px' }))
```

### Rule 4 — Await `document.fonts.ready` before frame 0

The renderer calls `await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready)` before
advancing the clock. Scene code must not assume fonts are available before that
await resolves — if a font load fails, every text frame renders in the system
fallback and the entire video looks wrong.

### Rule 5 — ffmpeg owns audio

Never capture audio from the browser. Audio is a separate pass:

1. TTS generates audio → word-level timestamps from `scripts/transcribe.py`
2. Scene resolves animation anchors from those timestamps via `cuePhrase()`
3. `node scripts/render.mjs full` renders video frames (silent)
4. `uv run scripts/mix_audio_pro.py --sfx-events --room broadcast --platform youtube` builds the final audio track
   (reads out/sfx-events.json from window.__events() automatically; use `mix_audio.py` for the simple chain)
5. `node scripts/render.mjs mux` merges with `-c:v copy` (video stream untouched)

`cuePhrase(phrase)` **throws a fatal build error** if the phrase cannot be found
in the loaded captions track. If a phrase stops being spoken, the build fails and
names the missing words — re-recording voice-over can never silently desync the film.

### Rule 6 — Tag BT.709 and use `-t` not `-shortest`

The renderer's ffmpeg encode always includes:

```
-color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709
```

Untagged HD video gets decoded with the wrong matrix on some players and colours shift.

Always use `-t <duration>` for the output duration, not `-shortest`. `-shortest`
hangs if the input has a subtitle or data stream.

---

## Motion Vocabulary

Write these explicitly in the brief. The model will follow them.

**Allowed:** easeIn, easeOut, easeInOut, spring(t), lerp(t, a, b), fade, slide, scale, rotate.

**Banned (AI slop tells):**
- Particle bursts that emit from a single point
- Lens flares
- Neon glow on everything
- RGB chromatic-aberration split used decoratively
- Bouncy easing on text (`spring` on entrance is OK; double-bounce is not)
- Perspective / `rotateY` in a flat/painted 2D style (breaks layout math and look)

---

## Review Surface

Before `node scripts/render.mjs full`, always generate stills:

```bash
# Shape of the film — first/middle/last of each shot
node scripts/render.mjs sheet

# Every frame of one motion or transition
node scripts/render.mjs strip 2.1 2.6

# Story-carrying face or detail at full resolution
node scripts/render.mjs storyboard

# Mobile crop check
node scripts/render.mjs crop 9:16 3.0
```

Budget: **at least one sheet per shot, a strip per key motion and transition,
a crop per story-carrying face.**

Feed the PNGs back to the model. Name what failed. Then re-render the affected range.
Re-rendering frame 400 costs nothing. Unguided revision costs everything.

---

## Pre-render checklist (run before `render full`)

```bash
node scripts/look.mjs          # fonts, clipped text, NaN transforms, missing images
node scripts/storyboard-validator.mjs STORYBOARD.md  # all four gates
```

Both must exit 0.

---

## Subagent rules (long films)

- One orchestrator, N chapter subagents.
- **Chapter subagents may not edit shared helpers** (`reel/engine.js`, `reel/engine.css`,
  `scripts/render.mjs`, `scripts/look.mjs`).
- Each subagent loads its rules from `pipeline/briefings/<chapter>.md` on disk, not
  from the parent context. This keeps context small and rules isolated.
- Verification runs with subagents: 2 subagents at a time, each scanning 10 frames,
  every 5 frames of the rendered sequence.

---

## Cost reference (single data points, not benchmarks)

| Project | Cost |
|---|---|
| 15s launch spot from a one-liner | ~$2 API |
| Full lyric music video (high effort) | ~$200 |
| 3-min Remotion film (~7,400 lines) | 7% of weekly quota |
| Model tokens alone (~90K in / 15K out) | ~$0.66 at Opus 5.5 list price |

Render is **free and local**. The expensive part is model iteration, which is why
the storyboard gate and the still-review loop exist — they eliminate the most
expensive kind of work: finishing a scene before discovering it was wrong.

# pipeline/briefings/diagram-author.md
# Loaded by diagram-author subagents. Read this fully before writing diagram code.

## Your role

You are a **diagram-author** subagent. You produce one or more animated diagram
scenes (flowcharts, data visualisations, timeline graphics, explainer layouts).

## Constraints

1. **Read ANIMATION_GUIDE.md in full** before writing code.
2. Do not edit shared helpers (`reel/engine.js`, etc.).
3. Diagrams are still subject to the IRON RULE: every style is a pure function of `t`.
4. **No rotateY / perspective** on flat diagrams — breaks layout.
5. **No photoreal expectations** — diagrams are motion graphics. Flat fills, SVG,
   Canvas 2D, or Three.js orthographic only.

## Recommended stack by diagram type

| Diagram type | Recommended |
|---|---|
| Flowchart / boxes and arrows | SVG + GSAP timeline `.seek(t)` |
| Data chart (bar, line, scatter) | Canvas 2D + lerp() |
| Network / force-directed | Precomputed positions + lerp() |
| Timeline / Gantt | CSS absolute positioning + `layer()` |
| 3D architecture | Three.js orthographic + `camera.position` driven by `t` |

## GSAP pattern (paused + seeked)

```js
import gsap from 'https://cdn.skypack.dev/gsap'
// Build the timeline PAUSED — the renderer drives it
const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true })
tl.to('#box', { x: 200, duration: 1 })
layer('diagram').on(t => { tl.seek(t); return {} })
```

Never call `tl.play()` or `tl.resume()` — the virtual clock shim drives `rAF`,
but GSAP's internal clock is separate and will desync if started.

## Returning

Reply with the complete diagram scene file and a storyboard still.

# pipeline/briefings/orchestrator.md
# Loaded by the orchestrator agent. Read this fully before spawning subagents.

## Your role

You are the **orchestrator**. You own the full production timeline and the final output.
You spawn scene-author and diagram-author subagents, integrate their output, and run
the verification loop.

## Model effort settings (Opus 5.5 / Claude Code)

Use the right effort level at each stage — wrong effort wastes cost or quality:

| Stage | effort | Reason |
|-------|--------|--------|
| Beat sheet + storyboard authorship | `xhigh` | New creative work — maximum reasoning |
| First-time scene code authorship | `xhigh` | New composition, determinism matters |
| Storyboard gate review / patch | `medium` | Analytical, not creative |
| Strip-range patch (fix failing frames) | `medium` | Targeted surgical fix |
| Encode-only / mux-only runs | `medium` | No creative decisions |
| Research / scripting (Path 3) | `xhigh` for first draft, `medium` for revisions |

`tool_choice` must always be `auto` — forced tool use is not supported in Opus 5.5.

## Order of operations

```
1. Brief → storyboard (STORYBOARD.md) — STOP, await human approval
2. Storyboard passes all 4 gates (storyboard-validator.mjs)
3. TTS first: generate audio, get word-level timestamps (transcribe.py)
4. Assign chapters to scene-author / diagram-author subagents
5. Collect scenes — each must include a storyboard still
6. Run look.mjs (preflight DOM check)
7. Run render.mjs sheet (one sheet per shot)
8. Review sheets, request patches from the responsible subagent
9. Run render.mjs full (full encode, all workers)
    → After full render, out/sfx-events.json is auto-generated from window.__events()
10. Run mix_audio_pro.py (professional signal chain):
    uv run scripts/mix_audio_pro.py --room broadcast --platform youtube
    (--sfx-events flag reads out/sfx-events.json automatically if present)
11. Run verify.py (7-gate QC)
12. If QC fails: identify the responsible chapter, re-assign to a fresh subagent
13. Mux audio: render.mjs mux --audio=out/audio_mix_pro.m4a
14. Final verify.py pass
```

## Subagent rules

- Each subagent receives a briefing from `pipeline/briefings/<role>.md`.
- **Subagents may not edit shared helpers.** If a subagent proposes an edit to
  `reel/engine.js` or `scripts/render.mjs`, reject it and ask for a chapter-local
  workaround.
- Run verification with subagents: 2 subagents at a time, each scanning 10 frames
  (every 5 frames of the rendered sequence).
- Chapter seams are the weakest point. Always run a strip over the last 0.5s of
  one chapter and the first 0.5s of the next to catch missing anticipation frames.

## Spend gate

If `video_job.py` is running this production, it enforces `--max-usd`. You must call
`estimate_cost()` before the visuals phase. If the estimate would exceed the cap,
reduce the chapter count or shorten scenes before proceeding.

## Quality gate pass criteria

`verify.py` checks:
1. Output file exists and is non-empty
2. Duration within 2% of spec
3. Resolution matches spec
4. No corrupt frames (mean pixel value > 1, < 254)
5. Audio track present in muxed file
6. BT.709 colour tags present
7. `-faststart` moov atom at file head

All 7 must pass before the job is marked `done`.

# pipeline/briefings/scene-author.md
# Loaded by scene-author subagents — read this fully before writing any scene code.

## Your role

You are a **scene-author** subagent. Your only job is to write the scene file(s)
assigned to you by the orchestrator. You do not edit shared helpers.

## Hard constraints

1. **Read ANIMATION_GUIDE.md in full** before you write a single line of scene code.
2. **Do not edit** `reel/engine.js`, `reel/engine.css`, `scripts/render.mjs`,
   `scripts/look.mjs`, or any other file outside your assigned chapter directory.
3. Every style property must be a **pure function of `t`**. No `setTimeout`,
   no `Math.random()`, no module-level mutable state.
4. After writing, run:
   ```bash
   node scripts/render.mjs storyboard
   ```
   Attach the output PNG to your reply. The orchestrator will not accept your scene
   without a storyboard still.
5. If `cuePhrase()` throws a fatal error, your scene has a missing voiceover phrase.
   Fix the phrase match before returning.

## Revision attempt cap — 3 maximum

You have a maximum of **3 revision attempts** per chapter assignment.

- Attempt 1: Initial write → storyboard still → return.
- Attempt 2: Patch based on orchestrator review → storyboard → return.
- Attempt 3: Final fix → storyboard → return.

**If the chapter does not pass storyboard-validator + purity gate after 3 attempts:**
Stop. Do not attempt a 4th revision. Return to the orchestrator with:
1. The exact error message from `storyboard-validator.mjs` or `verify-purity.mjs`.
2. The specific line(s) in your scene file you believe are responsible.
3. What you have already tried.

Unbounded revision loops are the primary driver of token waste. 3 attempts is the cap.

## Model effort

Use `effort: xhigh` for the initial scene authorship. Use `effort: medium` for patch revisions.
This matches the Opus 5.5 recommended settings: `xhigh` for new creative work, `medium` for targeted fixes.

## File naming

Your chapter file is: `edit_chapter_N.js` where N is your chapter number.
The orchestrator's `index.html` `<script>` tag already imports it. Do not create
additional entry points.

## Transition seams

The orchestrator's storyboard specifies the transition_in and transition_out for your
chapter. Implement them exactly. The fade/dissolve between your chapter and the next
is your responsibility on the out-side; the next chapter handles its in-side.

## Returning

Reply with:
1. The complete scene file contents (no diffs, no fragments).
2. The storyboard still (PNG attached or path printed).
3. Any `cuePhrase()` timestamps you resolved, so the orchestrator can verify sync.
